description:
## What changed

Nine new patches, a settings screen rebuilt around how people look for things, and a night of fixes for switches that had quietly stopped working.

**A Privacy page, and the device patches made true.** Everything that decides what TikTok learns sits on one page now: Disable analytics and tracking, Ghost mode, the three link rows, and a switch for each of the seven device patches (contact list, installed apps, location, clipboard, motion sensors, the in-app browser bridge and the camera and microphone dot). Three of those patches said more than they did and two did nothing at all. The contact blocker matched the wrong call form and intercepted zero sites; the installed-app blocker watched a call TikTok never makes. Both read the right sites now, every privacy patch refuses to apply when it finds nothing to intercept, and the camera dot draws the green and orange dot it promised, and takes it away again when the recorder closes.

**The right column switches work again.** The six switches that hide the like, comment, save, share, avatar and music buttons had looked for the video cell in the wrong place since 0.35.0 and hid nothing. They work on 46.2.3 again. Feed button size grows the icons by a quarter; the larger sizes offered before are gone because the column has no room for them.

**The settings menu is four groups.** Your feed, Watching and sharing, Privacy and system, and About, with Search settings in a card of its own above them. Screen time is its own page for the daily budgets, reminders and the hold, and Backup and restore is its own page for Back up, Restore, Reset and Undo. Five pages have shorter names: Feed screen, Feed tabs, Comments, Region and App. Inside the pages, rows sit under headings that say what they are about, and the right column's six hides are one checklist row that says what is hidden.

**Also.** Block P2P video relay and Stop on-device AI profiling. Maximum views per comment under Feed filter. The share prompt after a like can be hidden. The remembered playback speed can be turned off. Links in comments can be tapped. Text rows show their current value. The Feature Gate Lab speaks in plain terms. Hide Tako AI covers three more trigger components. The core asset strip no longer empties three libraries other libraries link against, which had crashed the Create tab.

**Checked on a phone, and four things fixed because of it.** An overnight pass on a Galaxy S22 running 46.2.3 exercised the comment sheet, downloads, the interaction switches, playback, the display shapes, the privacy hooks and the theme, switch by switch. It turned up four defects, all fixed here: Hide quick comment reactions never reached the emoji row above the comment box (it does now, after a restart, and its row says so); "Save the sound as well" failed on every video because TikTok's audio track starts before zero and the copy loop read that as the end; a hold on Like with the long-press repost disabled fell through to a like; and the core asset strip refused the newer TikTok builds. What passed: comment search, the keyword and user filters, the copy sanitizer, the share confirm step, the follow and like confirmations, both long-press switches, downloads with and without the watermark, without sound, at a chosen quality, with subtitles and with the profile picture, stop video looping, automatic advance, custom speeds, fit video to screen, the contact list blocker, the browser bridge guard and the AMOLED theme. What could not be shown on a phone: the foldable split comment view, which needs TikTok's tablet layout, and the location and clipboard hooks, which TikTok never called during the pass.

**Validation.** 1405 runtime tests and the patches module suite passed locally. The receipt attached below records every patch applying to the 46.2.3, 46.7.3, 46.8.3 and 46.9.3 fixtures with the real desktop CLI. Needs Morphe Manager 1.30.0 or newer.

The downloadable .mpp is the patch bundle. Patch on the device with Morphe Manager and keep its existing signing key.
